title: Applied anatomy: the pancreas and duodenum in pancreaticoduodenectomy

header.contentArea: Surgical anatomy: pancreas, duodenum and hepatobiliary surgery

related.why: The painless jaundice history that leads to this operation
Coeliac and gastroduodenal blood supply, shared with the pancreatic head

brief.scenario: Mr Sean Coultard, 62, presented with painless jaundice. CT shows a mass in the head of the pancreas with no vascular involvement and no metastases. The MDT has listed him for pancreaticoduodenectomy.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the anatomy of the pancreas and duodenum and its relevance to the operation.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Parts, relations, blood supply, then what the operation removes and what it endangers.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Forgetting that the head and duodenum share a blood supply, which is why they come out together.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "The head sits in the duodenal C-loop; the neck lies in front of the superior mesenteric and portal veins."

grid.label: Parts and position
grid.fail: Cannot name the head, uncinate process, neck, body and tail, or describe where the gland lies.
grid.pass: Head in the duodenal C-loop, uncinate process, neck, body and tail; retroperitoneal except the tail, which reaches the splenic hilum.
grid.high: Describes the four parts of the duodenum and the major papilla on the second part.

grid.label: Relations of the head and neck
grid.fail: Cannot describe what lies behind the head or neck.
grid.pass: Bile duct in a groove or tunnel on the posterior head; superior mesenteric and splenic veins join behind the neck to form the portal vein.
grid.high: Uncinate process passes behind the superior mesenteric vein; inferior vena cava and left renal vein lie posteriorly.

grid.label: Shared blood supply
grid.fail: Cannot name the arteries to the pancreatic head.
grid.pass: Superior pancreaticoduodenal arteries from the gastroduodenal, inferior from the superior mesenteric, forming arcades.
grid.high: Explains that the head and duodenum share these arcades, so the head cannot be removed without the duodenum.

grid.label: Vessels at risk and resectability
grid.fail: Cannot name the vessels at risk, or thinks any vein contact makes it unresectable.
grid.pass: Superior mesenteric vein and portal vein, superior mesenteric artery, common hepatic artery; resectability depends on tumour contact with these.
grid.high: Checks for a replaced right hepatic artery from the SMA, and test-clamps the gastroduodenal artery before dividing it.

grid.label: Classic versus pylorus-preserving
grid.fail: Cannot say what either operation removes.
grid.pass: Classic removes head, duodenum, distal stomach, gallbladder and distal bile duct; pylorus-preserving keeps the stomach and pylorus.
grid.high: Cites randomised evidence of no difference in mortality or survival, with more delayed gastric emptying after pylorus preservation.

grid.label: Reconstruction and aftercare
grid.fail: Cannot describe how continuity is restored.
grid.pass: Pancreaticojejunostomy, hepaticojejunostomy and gastro- or duodenojejunostomy; pancreatic fistula is the key complication.
grid.high: Operates rather than stents first if fit, and considers pancreatic enzyme replacement before and after resection.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Superior mesenteric and portal veins, superior mesenteric artery and common hepatic artery. Contact with these decides resectability.

pass.speaker: candidate
pass.text: Head, duodenum, distal stomach, gallbladder and distal bile duct. The pylorus-preserving version keeps the stomach.

pass.speaker: candidate

high.speaker: examiner
high.text: Describe the parts of the pancreas and where it lies.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Head, uncinate process, neck, body, tail. The duodenum is in four parts, with the major papilla on the second.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: It hooks behind the superior mesenteric vein. Behind the head lie the inferior vena cava and left renal vein.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: The head and duodenum share the pancreaticoduodenal arcades, so the head can't be removed without it.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: A replaced right hepatic artery from the superior mesenteric runs behind the head. I'd test-clamp the gastroduodenal and feel the hepatic pulse before dividing it.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: Randomised trials show no difference in mortality or survival, but more delayed gastric emptying with pylorus preservation.

high.speaker: candidate
high.text: If he's fit, operate rather than drain. I'd consider pancreatic enzyme replacement before and after.

failures.move: Not knowing the head and duodenum share a blood supply.
failures.consequence: Cannot explain why the duodenum is removed.

failures.move: Dividing the gastroduodenal artery without checking hepatic flow.
failures.consequence: A replaced or stenosed hepatic supply can be lost, causing liver ischaemia.

failures.move: Routinely stenting a fit jaundiced patient before resection.
failures.consequence: Delays surgery and adds stent complications.

recovery.when: You lose track of the vessels
recovery.line: Let me work from the neck: portal vein behind it, superior mesenteric vein below, artery to its left.
I'd quote our unit's audited results rather than a figure I can't source.

knowledge.fact: Portal vein forms behind the pancreatic neck; the uncinate process lies behind the superior mesenteric vein.
Head and duodenum share the superior (gastroduodenal) and inferior (superior mesenteric) pancreaticoduodenal arcades.
Resectability depends on tumour contact with the superior mesenteric and portal veins, superior mesenteric artery, coeliac axis and common hepatic artery.
Pylorus preservation: no mortality or survival difference; more delayed gastric emptying.
Resectable with jaundice and fit: resect rather than drain first. Consider pancreatin before and after resection.

recall.think: Portal vein or hepatic artery injury, and pancreatic fistula.
recall.say: "Head and duodenum share a blood supply, so they come out together."
do: Name head, uncinate, neck, body, tail
Check for a replaced right hepatic artery

numbers.meaning: Parts of the duodenum; papilla on the second

recall.trap: Any vein contact does not automatically mean unresectable.
recall.finish: Pancreaticoduodenectomy with three anastomoses in a specialist centre.

partner.opening: "This man is listed for a pancreaticoduodenectomy. Describe the parts of the pancreas and where it lies."
partner.actorBrief: You are the examiner. Start with the parts of the pancreas, then work down the push questions. Press for precise relations if answers are vague.

reveals.finding: Mass in the pancreatic head; clear fat plane around the superior mesenteric artery; no venous contact; no metastases.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks about jaundice and fitness
reveals.finding: Bilirubin rising; no cholangitis; fit for surgery.

push.question: What lies behind the neck of the pancreas?
push.expect: Superior mesenteric and splenic veins forming the portal vein.

push.question: Why must the duodenum come out with the head?
Which vessels decide resectability?
push.expect: SMV and portal vein, SMA, coeliac axis, common hepatic artery.

push.question: How is continuity restored?
push.expect: Pancreatico-, hepatico- and gastro- or duodenojejunostomy.

curveballs.safeAnswer: Declines an unsourced figure; lower in high-volume centres; quotes unit audit.

curveballs.prompt: After dividing the gastroduodenal artery the hepatic pulse disappears.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Suspects hepatic artery injury or stenosis; stop, assess, senior HPB surgeon and vascular repair.
Either is acceptable; no survival difference; more delayed gastric emptying with preservation.
